newsitem.title: USA: Seagull to sell N. America assets and look overseas.
newsitem.headline: Seagull to sell N. America assets and look overseas.

text.p: Seagull Energy Corp. on Wednesday joined the list of oil and gas companies selling North American resources and deploying assets overseas.

The company will sell its Canadian exploration and production operations, primarily natural gas reserves of 42.7 million barrels of oil equivalent on 375,000 developed acres, as well as an additional unexplored holding of 400,000 acres, mostly in the province of Alberta.
"The fact that prices for North American reserves have pushed up is a factor, but the primary reason is that we see better opportunities overseas," said Seagull spokesman Alan Payne.
The company plans to invest most of the proceeds of the sale in its rapidly expanding operations in Egypt.
Seagull's move comes hard on the heels of a decision by Amoco Corp. to sell 15 percent of its U.S. reserves and invest the money overseas, where it too sees better opportunities than North America.
Canada has also been a hot place for oil and gas deals, as Amerada Hess sold its Canadian assets to Petro-Canada for C$730 million and Wainoco Oil Corp. sold to Numac Energy Inc. for C$133.6 million.

"All kinds of people are looking at properties, from royalty trusts to aggressive buyers such as Canadian 88 Energy Corp., Gulf Canada Resources Ltd., Talisman and Canadian Occidental Petroleum Ltd.," said Scott Inglis, analyst at FirstEnergy Capital Corp in Calgary.
He said that Seagull's proven reserves alone could be worth C$350 million (US$250 million), while Painewebber analyst Ron Barone said they would be worth at least US$200 million.

Seagull shares closed 37.5 cents lower at $17.875 on the New York Stock Exchange in the wake of the divestment plans, in line with a generally weaker market for independent U.S. exploration and production companies.

Unlike Amoco, which is selling properties that are far more expensive to operate than the company average, extraction costs for the Seagull reserves are $3.04 per barrel of oil equivalent, close to the $3.03 company average.
Seagull's main focus of operation is in Egypt, where it has a joint venture with Apache Corp.

On Tuesday, Seagull said it had successfully completed a well on its wholly owned South Hurghada site in Egypt and it plans to start trucking out oil later this year at a rate of 800 barrels per day, rising to 4,000 by the end of the year.
The company is also producing from its Qarun field in Egypt at the rate of 40,000 barrels per day.
